text:
alex: Hey team — customer reported a sudden spike of 429s after a backend deploy. They said errors shifted between "auth 429" and generic rate-limit 429s. Affected model: rwd-large-64k (only on that model/route). Repro steps and logs below, any quick ideas?

maya: Can you paste the raw error body and the request headers (no private keys, just header names and lengths)? Also which endpoint?

alex: Here's a sanitized curl we got from the customer: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-64k","input":"<~131072 bytes context>","max_tokens":512}'
```
Response body they attached: 
```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_error",
    "message": "Rate limit exceeded: per-model concurrent requests (16) exceeded for rwd-large-64k",
    "code": 429
  }
}
```
They also saw an earlier variant: 
```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "auth_error",
    "message": "429 indirect: auth quota checkpoint hit - billing backend returned 429",
    "code": 429
  }
}
```

jordan: Two things stand out: 1) large context (64k) multiplies token accounting so TPM blows up, and 2) the runtime has a smaller concurrency cap for this model because of KV cache pressure. rwd-large-64k currently has a soft per-API-key limit of 12 concurrent requests and a per-minute token cap of ~1.2M tokens (customer hit sustained bursts).

ops-bot: automated note: deployment rwd-runtime-v3 rolled to prod @ 2026-03-15T09:12:03Z — new kernel path enabled for 64k contexts. No incident flagged.

maya: Do we have metrics for that customer id? Specifically: requests/sec, concurrent inflight, and tokens/min for the 30m window around the spike. Also, were they using streaming (which can increase concurrent sessions)?

alex: Customer provided per-minute summary: 14 req/s sustained for ~10m, average input tokens ~98k (after encoding), plus 512 output -> tokens/min ≈ 85k * 60 = 5.1M tokens/min. They expected per-model TPM to be higher.

jordan: That token math explains it — 5.1M TPM >> our documented soft cap for rwd-large-64k (1.2M TPM). When a key exceeds TPM or concurrency we return 429. The auth 429 variant is from our billing gateway rejecting elevated token accounting checks (we surface as auth-ish).

samantha: Quick repro steps I ran locally: hit the rwd-large-64k with 10 parallel clients, each sending a 60k-token context every 6s. After ~90s we saw per-key TPM counters trigger and started getting 429s that matched the customer's timeline. I included traces: 
- trace_id: trace-08a3f
- worker: gpu-03b
- kernel: kv-enabled-v3

maya: Suggested immediate mitigations for the customer: reduce concurrency to <=8 for that model, batch multiple short contexts rather than many long single contexts, and switch to rwd-medium-32k if the extra context isn't strictly required. Also add exponential backoff (start 500ms, *2, cap 10s) and jitter.

alex: Customer also reported intermittent "auth billing" 429s when we retried quickly. Looks like rapid retries tripped the billing gateway TTL protections. We recommended single-point exponential backoff to avoid cascading 429s from both runtime and billing.

jordan: Ops next steps: 1) check whether the soft concurrency cap for rwd-large-64k should be temporarily increased in the region for this customer given committed capacity, 2) confirm billing gateway logs for that API key to see combined rejection reasons, 3) add a clearer error variant so customers can distinguish "per-model concurrency" vs "billing throttle".

ops-bot: ticket created: #INC-7321 linked to this thread (owner: eng-infra).

maya: I'll draft a short support reply with repro summary, suggested mitigations, and ask for permission to run a short load test (we'll coordinate time window).

alex: Thanks — customer accepted the mitigations and reduced parallelism. After moving to concurrency=6 and switching some calls to rwd-medium-32k they saw 429s stop. ops please follow up on increasing capacity or adding docs about model-specific TPM/RPS for 64k-context models. :thumbsup:

samantha: Noted — I'll add a doc snippet to the portal that lists per-model soft caps and examples of how context size affects TPM. Will push a PR to docs repo later today.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: docs/pr-3185 merged to main (will publish in next release).

alex: Closing loop — customer happy for now, leaving inc open until infra confirms whether capacity bump or clearer error codes will be implemented.
